newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ABC retains stake in Seven's Australia TV.
newsitem.headline: ABC retains stake in Seven's Australia TV.

text.p: The government-owned Australian Broadcasting Corp (ABC) said on Thursday it would retain a preference shareholding in Australia Television Pty Co Ltd and have two members on the five member board of the company.
Television broadcaster the Seven Network Ltd announced earlier it had bought Australia Television for an undisclosed amount.
Australia Television was set up four years ago to broadcast ABC programmes via satellite into Asia, partly funded by advertising.
Seven would meet all of Australia TV's operating costs and had guaranteed to maintain an Australian content-based service of 16 hours a day minimum for at least four and a half years.
ABC Chairman Donald McDonald told ABC radio the purchase price was somewhere under A$10 million, but he would not elaborate any further.
The ABC had a contract with Seven to provide the same news, current affairs and general programming currently provided to Australia Television, McDonald said.
The Australia Television's news bulletin would be the centrepiece of the new service and the ABC would retain editorial control, he said.
The ABC called for expressions of interest in Australia Television in December 1996 and received 50 responses, although only five conducted due diligence.
Earlier Seven announced that the purchase of Australia Television underpinned Seven's plans for the development of a significant presence in Asia.

Australia Television currently provides a free-to-air English language satellite television service covering most of the Asia Pacific region, reaching from Beijing in China in the north to Western Samoa in the east and India in the west.

It is currently being distributed to about 500 hotels throughout Asia and to various private and government residences through cable, land-based broadcasters and through direct-to-home satellite reception.
It had a potential audience of about 20 million homes and an audience base of three million, 500,000 of whom were Australian ex-patriates.

Seven Managing Director Gary Rice said the introduction of digital technology, coupled with Australia Television's extensive satellite delivery abilities, would allow Seven to broaden its Asian programming.
Australia Television transmits on the Palapa C2 satellite which beams signals across the Asia Pacific region and has an option for another nine year lease to that space.
It can also be extended digitally to take a total of six to eight channels.
